title: Representation in media texts
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:49Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point teaches context in novels for senior VCE students, while the new point is about how news stories and advertisements represent people and events, which is a different idea at a different depth.

draft.title: Representation in media texts
card: A media text does not show the world exactly as it is. It represents people, places and events: the maker chooses how to present them.
a report on an event. The maker chooses the headline, the images, the sources quoted and the words used to describe people.
a text made to sell a product or idea. It often shows people and places in an attractive way that suits the product.
These choices reflect the values and context of the makers, such as who they are, who their audience is and when and where they work. Two makers can represent the same thing in different ways.
draft.remember: Media makers choose how to show people, places and events, and those choices reflect their values and context.

a.q: What does it mean to say a news story represents an event?
opts: The maker chooses how to present the event
The story copies the event exactly as it happened
The story only includes events that the maker saw
The story shows the event the same way as other reports
a.why: Representation means the maker shapes how something is shown, through choices such as images, sources and words. It is wrong to say a story copies an event exactly, because the maker always makes choices.
a.clue: Think about the choices a maker has to make.

b.q: An ad for a holiday resort in Cairns shows only sunny beaches and smiling families. Which explanation best fits this representation of the place?
opts: The maker chose images that suit the aim of selling holidays
The maker had no choice because Cairns is always sunny
The maker wanted to give a full and balanced view of Cairns
The maker showed Cairns the way every other ad shows it
b.why: An advertisement is made to sell, so its maker picks attractive images that suit that purpose. The idea that the maker had no choice is wrong, because all makers decide what to show, and this ad is not a balanced view.
b.clue: Ask what the maker of an advertisement wants the audience to do.

a.best: The maker chooses how to present the event

b.best: The maker chose images that suit the aim of selling holidays
